Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Redwood CSM), Samantha Ortiz (Atlas Head of ML), Devon Park (Atlas Cloud Eng), Liam Chen (Atlas PM), Aisha Mbaye (Atlas Security)

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: all right everybody thanks for joining, lets get started. um quick roll call?
00:08 Samantha: hi sam here.
00:09 Devon: devon here.
:11 Liam: liam here.
00:13 Jordan: great, so agenda — onboarding status, access, results from the small benchmark maya ran, then next steps. maya, you wanna kick off with the benchmark?
00:25 Maya: yeah sure, uh so i ran the 1k and 2k token scenarios yesterday on our hosted env, i used the t5-ish open model we discussed and a quantized runner. results were: p50 latency about 210 ms for 1k tokens, p95 around 480 ms, cost looked like ~0.9 cents per request in this test. caveat — this was on low concurrency, single-worker, not real traffic.
00:58 Devon: when you say quantized, what precision? 8-bit or 4-bit?
01:02 Maya: 8-bit quantization. we did a quick 4-bit but kernel mismatch caused flakiness so we reverted for the report. also we had prefix caching disabled so kv cache not exercised.
01:18 Samantha: the p95 seems ok but we care about tail when we ramp. what's our options to shave the tail?
01:25 Maya: couple levers — batching higher concurrency helps throughput but can add latency for single-request flows; prefix/KV cache for repeated context cuts p95 a lot; also model variant (smaller decoder) can trade quality for cost and latency.
01:40 Liam: do we have an estimate on cost if we enable caching?
01:43 Maya: rough ballpark is 20-30% token cost reduction for repeated prompts over a session, depends on overlap. i'll include sim spreadsheet.
01:51 Priya: on the onboarding front, jordan, where are we with credentials and network?
01:55 Jordan: i have the onboarding doc drafted, i'll share after the call. main blockers are VPC peering and service account permissions. devon, any updates from your side?
02:06 Devon: we spun up a test VPC, but we need the exact peering CIDR and the ports that redwood will use; and our security team needs the SOC2 + encryption-at-rest details.
02:19 Aisha: yes please share encryption model and KMS details. we need to validate key management and audit logs.
02:26 Jordan: absolutely — we'll send SOC2 attestation, brief on KMS integrations, and network checklist. note: for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted we have envelope encryption with a customer key option.
02:42 Samantha: quick question on SSO — can we use our SAML IdP for access to the console?
02:47 Priya: yes Atlas can use SAML, we support SSO and RBAC. there are some config steps but that's standard.
02:55 Maya: on the technical deep-dive, i also wanted to mention batching and autoscale. for the poc we recommend a small dedicated pool and enable burst capacity; that reduces cold start jitter. also we can set up a canary policy to fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes.
03:17 Liam: ok sounds good. what about data residency? we're mostly us-east but some customers require EU residency.
03:23 Jordan: for this POC we're fine in us-east; we can discuss region pinning for production.
03:28 Devon: before we proceed, can redwood run a benchmark that mimics our traffic? we have a mix of short and long prompts and about 200 rps peak.
03:35 Maya: yes, if you can share a sanitized sample trace and request distribution i'll run a 2-hour benchmark with the quantized model and KV cache toggled.
03:44 Samantha: we'll prepare that. also we need to check data retention — logs must be retained for 90 days and we need audit hooks.
03:50 Jordan: noted. audit logs are part of the security pack i'll send. we also have per-token cost breakdowns in the console for visibility.
03:59 Maya: quick note on the 4-bit caveat — some GPU kernels aren't stable on our infra; when quantizing to 4-bit we sometimes see decoding errors. for production i recommend 8-bit with model distillation if needed.
04:11 Devon: ok thanks. for the VPC peering, what's the network port list?
04:15 Jordan: i'll include the minimal egress ports and IP ranges in the checklist; typically we need outbound to redwood endpoints on 443, and some healthcheck ports if you opt for private peering.
04:26 Aisha: and do you have options for private deployment? we may want an air-gapped option for certain clients.
04:31 Jordan: yes we have Redwood Private offering with on-prem package; that'll be a separate convo but we can intro the PM for that if needed.
04:40 Liam: okay let's recap next steps. Jordan to share security pack and onboarding doc; devon to provide peering details and create a service account; maya to run representative benchmark; sam to share sanitized sample trace.
04:56 Jordan: perfect. any blockers on timing? we suggested canary run on wednesday the 19th — does that work?
05:02 Samantha: that works for us.
05:04 Devon: yes.
05:06 Jordan: great, i'll send a calendar invite for the canary run and share the docs by friday.
05:12 Priya: i'll log action items in the playbook and follow up on SSO steps.
05:18 Maya: one last thing — i added a small set of tuning recommendations to the shared spreadsheet: batch size ranges, quantization profiles, kv cache TTL suggestions. i'll attach it with the benchmark results.
05:30 Samantha: thanks everyone. that was helpful.
05:33 Jordan: awesome, thanks all. meeting adjourned.
